_fictional: FICTIONAL GOLDEN SET. Every article, headline, claim, outlet, URL, figure, quotation, official body and fact-checker named in this file is INVENTED for Re-Vera's evaluation harness. Nothing here is real reporting, no real organisation said any of it, and every URL points at a reserved example domain so nothing can resolve to a real story. Never present any line of this file, or any output derived from it, as real reporting.

quote: rise by 40% from 1 January
notes: The article's headline figure. An official release and an independent outlet both put the median adjustment at 4 per cent, so the rules reach `contradicted` on a primary source that outweighs no support at all.

quote: More than 200 stalls have already closed this year
notes: Genuinely no evidence: retrieval finds nothing, so no model call is made at all and the claim must come back `unverifiable` with an explanation and no sources.

quote: The last islandwide rent adjustment took effect in 2024
notes: Two independent outlets on different domains — the brief's bar for `supported` without a primary source.

quote: eight in ten hawkers are considering leaving
notes: True but misleading, and the flagship case for the rules overruling the judge: the judge answers `supported`, the survey passage states 42 self-selected respondents, and aggregation weakens the verdict to `missing_context`.

quote: will not be capped under any circumstances
notes: A misquotation. The cited-source provider fetches the doorstop transcript, which is a primary source and says something else entirely.

quote: The review takes effect on 1 January
notes: One primary source is enough for `supported` under the brief's rule. The passage sits on a government domain, which is how aggregation recognises it.

quote: the adjustment is the first since 2019
notes: KNOWN MISS, kept deliberately. The evidence refutes the claim and the judge answers `contradicted`, but the only span it quotes is “since 2024” — ten characters, below judge.MIN_CITED_SPAN_CHARS (12) — so the citation is discarded and the claim is downgraded to `unverifiable`. A human labeller says contradicted; the pipeline abstains. This is the documented cost of that threshold (app/pipeline/judge.py, deviation 4), and it fails in the safe direction: recall on `contradicted` suffers, precision does not.

quote: delays on the East-West Line doubled in 2025
notes: A numeric claim refuted by official data — the data.gov.sg-shaped provider path.

quote: the line ran 1.2 million train-kilometres between delays
notes: Supported by the operator's own published figure on a government domain.

quote: the operator said the network is “the least reliable in the region”
notes: A second misquotation, this time inverting the speaker's meaning. The transcript is fetched as a cited source.

quote: nine in ten commuters said they were late at least once a week
notes: A true-but-misleading poll figure: the poll page states 60 self-selected respondents, so the small-sample signal fires and the verdict weakens.

quote: A new signalling upgrade begins in March
notes: Nothing retrieved. The honest answer, and the one that costs no tokens at all.

quote: punctuality improved in every quarter of 2025
notes: KNOWN MISS, kept deliberately. The statement is true and two independent outlets report it, so the rules reach `supported` and the judge agrees. It is also cherry-picked: the improvement is measured against a 2024 baseline depressed by a month-long shutdown, which no passage states as a number and no rule can see. Cherry-picking is the one true-but-misleading signal aggregation cannot detect (app/pipeline/aggregate.py) — it reaches a reader only if the judge spots it in the prose, and here the judge did not. A human labeller says missing_context; the pipeline says supported.

quote: resale flat prices jumped 30% in a single quarter
notes: Official index data refutes the headline figure by an order of magnitude.

quote: More than 1,000 flats crossed the million-dollar mark last year
notes: Two independent outlets on different domains agree on the figure — the ordinary `supported` shape, with a number specific enough that a wrong one would be obvious.

quote: buyers now wait seven years on average
notes: A survey figure with a 38-person sample. Supported in the sense that the survey says it, misleading in the sense that the survey cannot carry it.

quote: an agency spokesperson called the market “out of control”
notes: A third misquotation, and the one whose words are least like the original.

quote: The scheme opens for applications next month
notes: A forward-looking administrative detail with no published trace. Nothing found.

quote: dengue cases have tripled since January
notes: Official surveillance figures put the rise at 18 per cent.

quote: The agency has declared 40 active clusters
notes: One primary source on a government domain, matching the figure exactly.

quote: one in three households has stagnant water
notes: A striking ratio drawn from 55 homes in one estate. The supporting report is real; the generalisation is not.

quote: A new dengue vaccine will be offered free from July
notes: A consequential health claim with nothing behind it. Abstention is the product's correct answer, not a failure of it.

quote: Cases usually peak between June and October
notes: Background context, corroborated by two independent sources.

quote: The otter population has grown to about 200
notes: The wire-copy-only case. Three domains carry the identical agency story, so de-duplication collapses them into one source and the claim cannot reach the two independent sources `supported` requires. The judge answers `supported` and is overruled.

quote: Otters caused $2 million in fish-farm losses last year
notes: A published fact-check already exists, so retrieval short-circuits: the web-search bucket below is recorded and must never be reached. A ClaimReview refutation counts as strong on its own, which is the asymmetry the brief asks for.

quote: a park ranger said otters “should be culled”
notes: A fourth misquotation, attributing a policy position to someone who argued the opposite.

quote: Otters are protected under the Wildlife Act
notes: A legal fact stated by the responsible agency — one primary source, which is enough.

quote: screen time among teenagers has risen 400% since 2020
notes: A digital-literacy claim about digital literacy. The published study puts the rise at 34 per cent.

quote: Every secondary school now runs a digital literacy module
notes: Two independent outlets, no primary source — the ordinary `supported` shape.

quote: Half of students say they cannot tell real news from fake
notes: The fact-checker's own rating carries the signal here: a ClaimReview rated “Partly true” says the claim needs context, and aggregation reads that rating rather than a model's impression. The rating is never shown to a reader as a verdict.

quote: a ministry spokesperson said the curriculum is “a failure”
notes: The last misquotation in the set, and the one a reader is most likely to spread.

quote: The programme is funded until 2030
notes: A funding horizon nobody has published. Nothing retrieved, so nothing claimed.
